problem:
A random variable $X$ has the probability distribution given below.

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $0.25$ | $0.6$ | $0.1$ | $0.05$ |

Calculate $\text{E}[{X}^{4}].$

feedback.problem:
A random variable $X$ has the probability distribution given below.

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $0.4$ | $0.5$ | $0$ | $0.1$ |

Calculate $\text{E}[{X}^{4}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
If $X$ is a discrete random variable with probability mass function $f(x)$ and sample space $S,$ the expected value of ${X}^{4}$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{4}]={\sum }_{x\in S}{x}^{4}\cdot f(x).
$$

Summing up the products of each squared value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{4}] & ={\sum }_{x\in S}{x}^{4}\cdot f(x) \\  & ={1}^{4}\cdot 0.4+{2}^{4}\cdot 0.5+{3}^{4}\cdot 0+{4}^{4}\cdot 0.1 \\  & =1\cdot 0.4+16\cdot 0.5+81\cdot 0+256\cdot 0.1 \\  & =0.4+8+0+25.6 \\  & =34.\end{aligned}
$$
